2027-04-19.alt: Season of the Resurrection (Qyamta). The fourth week of the Resurrection begins, the day after the Sunday of prayer for vocations. The Gospel stops at verse 16; the saying about the rejected stone follows at once in verse 17.
2027-04-19.verse: Then the owner of the vineyard said, ‘What shall I do? I will send my beloved son; perhaps they will respect him.’
theo: Paul is near the end of his first letter to Timothy, the young bishop of Ephesus, and he gathers everything into one solemn charge. He does not give it in his own name alone. He calls two witnesses into the room: “In the presence of God, who gives life to all things, and of Christ Jesus, who in his testimony before Pontius Pilate made the good confession, I charge you to keep the commandment without spot or blame until the manifestation of our Lord Jesus Christ.” The first witness is the God who gives life to all things: in this Easter season we hear that name with new ears, for the God who gives life is the God who raised Jesus from the tomb. The second witness is Jesus standing before Pilate. He was bound, mocked and alone, and yet he spoke the truth calmly: he was a king, and his kingdom was not from this world. That quiet answer is what Paul calls “the good confession”. One verse earlier Paul reminded Timothy that he too had made the good confession “in the presence of many witnesses”, most likely on the day of his Baptism. Every Christian has stood where Timothy stood. At the font we, or our godparents for us, renounced Satan and confessed the faith; at every Holy Qurbana we confess it again in the Creed. Paul's charge is that we keep that confession clean until the Lord appears.

Then the letter breaks into praise, as if Paul cannot mention the coming of Christ without singing. God “will bring about at the right time” the appearing of his Son: “he who is the blessed and only Sovereign, the King of kings and Lord of lords. It is he alone who has immortality and dwells in unapproachable light, whom no one has ever seen or can see; to him be honor and eternal dominion. Amen.” These lines sound like a hymn the Church at Ephesus already sang. They tell us two things at once. God is utterly beyond us: no eye can bear his light, no mind can hold him. And yet this same God has made himself known, for the One who stood before Pilate is the image of the invisible God. In the Risen Christ the unapproachable light has come near. On Easter evening the disciples touched him and ate with him. Our Syro-Malabar Qurbana keeps both truths in its prayers: it adores the hidden majesty of God with deep bows and veiled gifts, and in the same celebration it gives us the Body and Blood of the Lord to eat and drink. Holy fear and holy nearness belong together.

In the Gospel Jesus tells a parable in the Temple during his last days in Jerusalem. A man plants a vineyard, leases it to tenants and goes away. At harvest he sends a slave for his share, then a second, then a third; each is beaten and sent away empty-handed. “Then the owner of the vineyard said, ‘What shall I do? I will send my beloved son; perhaps they will respect him.’” The tenants reason coldly: “This is the heir; let us kill him so that the inheritance may be ours.” They throw him out of the vineyard and kill him. Jesus tells this story a few days before he himself is led outside the city wall to be crucified. The parable is aimed at the leaders who were plotting against him, and Luke says they understood it; it is not a charge against the Jewish people, whom the Church honours as the first tenants of God's vineyard and to whom God's gifts and calling remain irrevocable. The story is a mirror for us. The vineyard is now the Church, and we are its tenants. God still sends his messengers, still asks for the fruit of faith, mercy and justice. The rejected Son is now the Risen Son: the very next line of the Gospel recalls the psalm, “The stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone.” Easter is God's answer to the tenants. What men threw out of the vineyard, God set at the corner of a new house, and he has given that house to us. The question for this Monday is simple: when the Owner sends for the fruit, what will he find in my part of the vineyard?
conn: Jesus before Pilate: “For this I was born, and for this I came into the world, to testify to the truth” (John 18:37); Timothy made his own confession “in the presence of many witnesses” (1 Timothy 6:12).
Revelation calls Jesus “the faithful witness, the firstborn of the dead” (Revelation 1:5): the one who confessed the truth before Pilate is the first to rise.
God is “wrapped in light as with a garment” (Psalm 104:2); yet “the light shines in the darkness” (John 1:5), and the glory of God shines “in the face of Jesus Christ” (2 Corinthians 4:6).
Isaiah sang of God's vineyard that yielded wild grapes (Isaiah 5:1–7); Jesus takes up the same image in this parable.
At the Jordan the Father says, “You are my Son, the Beloved” (Luke 3:22); in the parable the owner sends “my beloved son”.
“The stone that the builders rejected has become the chief cornerstone” (Psalm 118:22), quoted by Jesus (Luke 20:17) and by Peter after the Resurrection (Acts 4:11).
altar: At the Holy Qurbana we repeat the good confession in the Creed, and the Son who was thrown out of the vineyard comes to us as the living Bread. The fruit the Father seeks is offered on the altar with the Son's own offering.
The God who dwells in unapproachable light gives himself in the humble form of bread and wine: we approach with reverence and we receive with love.

live: Find your Baptism date this week, and on that day say the Creed slowly as your own good confession.
When you are tempted to lie to escape trouble, remember Jesus before Pilate and say what is true, with gentleness.
Choose one fruit you can give God this week: an hour of prayer, an act of mercy, a gift to the poor.
Make a slow, reverent bow when you enter the church: God dwells in light, and he lets us come near.
fathers: God planted the vineyard of the human race, first in creation and then in choosing a people. He sent the prophets, and at last his own Son. The vineyard was not destroyed but handed on: now it is fenced by the Church and spread throughout the world, and the same God asks from us the fruit he always asked.

See the patience of the owner. After the first servant was beaten, he sent a second; after the second, a third; after them all, his Son. He did not stop sending because they refused. So God deals with each of us: he does not tire of calling, and we must not tire of answering.
magis: Before Pilate, Christ proclaims that he came into the world to bear witness to the truth; the Christian is not to be ashamed of testifying to the Lord.
Martyrdom is the supreme witness given to the truth of the faith: it means bearing witness even unto death.
The Church is a cultivated field, the tillage of God; she is the choice vineyard planted by the heavenly cultivator, and Christ is the true vine.
The responsibility for the trial and death of Jesus cannot be laid on all the Jews of that time or of today; all sinners were the authors of Christ's Passion.
The Creed, our profession of faith, is recalled each Sunday: the faith confessed at Baptism is renewed in the liturgy.
saints: 19–25 April: fourth week of the Resurrection. Wed 21: in the Latin calendar, St Anselm. Fri 23: in the Latin calendar, St George. Sat 24: in the Syro-Malabar calendar, St George, Martyr (Geevarghese Sahada), an important feast. Sun 25: Fifth Sunday of Resurrection, with Mar Addai; St Mark the Evangelist (25 Apr) gives way to the Sunday this year (verify locally).
2027-04-19.prayer: God our Father, you give life to all things, and you raised your beloved Son whom the builders rejected. Make us faithful tenants of your vineyard, the Church. Keep our baptismal confession clean until the appearing of our Lord, give us courage to speak the truth as he spoke it before Pilate, and let our lives bear the fruit you seek. To you, King of kings and Lord of lords, who dwell in unapproachable light, be honour and eternal dominion, with your Son and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen. Alleluia!

catechism: No collective blame for the Passion.
kidsaint: Timothy was a young man when Paul chose him as a helper. His grandmother Lois and his mother Eunice taught him the Scriptures when he was a child. Paul made him the leader of the Church in Ephesus and wrote him letters full of advice. Lesson: what you learn about Jesus at home can make you a helper of the whole Church!

term: Paul's name for a public statement of faith made before witnesses. Jesus made it before Pilate; Timothy made it, probably at his Baptism; every Christian makes it at Baptism and renews it in the Creed. In Greek the word is homologia, ‘saying the same thing’: saying with our lips what God has said to us.

family.explain: Jesus told a story about a man who planted a lovely vineyard and let some farmers look after it. When it was time for the grapes, he sent helpers to collect his share, but the farmers were rude and sent them away. At last he sent his own dear son. The farmers did a very bad thing to him. Jesus was telling us about himself: God sent his Son, and people did not welcome him. But God raised Jesus from the dead! Now God has given us his vineyard, the Church, to look after.
family.intention: We pray for all the people who look after God's Church: our bishop, our priests, our parents and our teachers.
family.ask: Ask: “What good fruit can we give God this week? Let us choose one kind thing to do together.”

illus: A farmer near Thodupuzha inherited a small rubber and pepper garden from his father. For years he left it to a caretaker and visited only to collect the money. When the caretaker grew careless, the vines withered and the trees were tapped badly. The farmer's son, home from the Gulf, began to walk through the garden every morning before work, clearing weeds and tying up the pepper vines. Within two seasons the garden was giving fruit again. The father said, “It was always the same land. What changed was that someone loved it enough to tend it.” The vineyard of the Church is like that: it gives fruit where someone tends it each day with love.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, beloved Son of the Father, rejected by the builders and raised as the cornerstone, gather us now in your vineyard and teach us to bear fruit. Amen. Alleluia!
share: Christ Jesus, who in his testimony before Pontius Pilate made the good confession (1 Timothy 6:13). When have I found it hard to speak the truth about my faith?
He dwells in unapproachable light (1 Timothy 6:16). How do I show reverence for God in prayer and in church?
I will send my beloved son; perhaps they will respect him (Luke 20:13). Where has God sent messengers into my life, and how have I received them?
The stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone (Psalm 118:22). Where have I seen God bring good out of rejection?
pm.resp: Lord, make us fruitful in your vineyard.
interc: For our bishops and priests, the tenants God has placed over his vineyard, that they may be faithful and generous.
For all who are called to the priesthood and religious life, that they may answer with courage.
For Christians who suffer for the faith, that they may make the good confession with the peace of Christ.
For the Jewish people, the first to hear the word of God, that he may bless them in his faithfulness.
For our families and parishes, that they may bear the fruit of faith, mercy and justice.
pm.close: Father, you sent your beloved Son into the vineyard, and when he was rejected you raised him to be the cornerstone. Make us faithful in our confession and fruitful in our works, until he comes again in glory. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

homily: Dear friends, on this Monday of the fourth week of Easter, Paul gives Timothy a solemn charge, and Jesus tells a story that is hard to forget.

Paul calls two witnesses: the God who gives life to all things, and Christ Jesus, who made the good confession before Pilate. Jesus stood bound and alone, and spoke the truth calmly. Timothy made his own good confession at his Baptism. So did we. Paul's charge is for us too: keep that confession clean until the Lord comes.

Then Paul sings: God is “the King of kings and Lord of lords”, who “dwells in unapproachable light”. No one can see him. And yet in the Risen Christ that light has come near: the disciples touched him and ate with him. In the Holy Qurbana we bow before the hidden majesty of God, and we receive the Lord himself.

In the Gospel the owner of the vineyard sends servant after servant, and at last he says: “I will send my beloved son; perhaps they will respect him.” They kill him. Jesus told this story days before he was led outside the city to die. It was a warning to those who plotted against him; it is a mirror for us.
Today we are the tenants. The vineyard is the Church. God still asks for fruit: faith, mercy, justice. And God has answered the tenants with Easter: the rejected stone has become the cornerstone.
So let us ask ourselves today: what fruit will the Owner find in my part of the vineyard? Let us give him a good share this week. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus told a story about a vineyard. The owner sent his own dear son, but the farmers did not welcome him. Jesus was talking about himself!
God has given us his vineyard, the Church, to look after. Every kind thing you do is a sweet grape for God!
